displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that objective morality consists of empirically answerable principles governing the flourishing of rational, socially interdependent agents whose agency requires reciprocal protection.

novelty.explanation: This formulation repairs the missing normative and interpersonal bridges by making rational agency and reciprocal social dependence explicit.

premises.text: Living rational agents possess constitutive needs for cognition, purposive action, bodily integrity, cooperation, and long-term planning, and frustration of these needs predictably impairs their flourishing.

novelty.explanation: This extends the life standard by specifying several empirically assessable components of flourishing.

premises.text: Because human flourishing depends upon stable interaction with other independent agents, principles authorizing opportunistic coercion undermine the general conditions upon which each person's agency relies.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed transition from individual requirements to interpersonal constraints and directly addresses advantageous wrongdoing.

premises.text: A moral principle is objective when its application depends upon publicly assessable facts about agency and flourishing rather than upon a speaker's momentary approval or emotional intensity.

novelty.explanation: This develops the relational account of objectivity into a more explicit criterion of truth and application.

premises.text: Sentient nonhuman animals can be moral patients without being moral agents because suffering, preference, and vulnerability provide life-relevant reasons for protection even when reciprocal responsibility is impossible.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the inference from animals' nonagency to rightlessness by separating moral agency from moral-patient status.

conclusion.text: Therefore, facts about flourishing can support defeasible objective duties protecting agency, reciprocal freedom, and sentient welfare, although their precise scope requires continuing empirical and philosophical specification.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion preserves the life-centered direction while limiting its claim to defeasible duties supported by the strengthened premises.

newArguments.title: Constitutive agency test
newArguments.text: Instead of asking whether a murderer happens to profit on one occasion, evaluate the maxim authorizing that conduct as a principle for agents who depend upon stable recognition of planning, bodily security, evidence, and voluntary cooperation. A permission for advantageous killing selectively exempts the actor from conditions that make rational social agency possible. The objection is therefore not merely that murder usually backfires, but that opportunistic coercion contradicts the reciprocal framework the actor invokes whenever claiming authority over personal judgment and action.

novelty.explanation: This is a new constitutive-consistency argument connecting individual agency to reciprocal constraints without relying on ordinary prudential consequences.

newArguments.title: Patienthood without agency
newArguments.text: Moral agency and moral patienthood answer different questions: who can deliberate about principles, and whose condition supplies reasons for deliberators. Animals may lack responsibility while still possessing welfare, aversive experience, preferences, and vulnerability to purposeless injury. A life-centered framework can therefore condemn torture because it destroys an objectively identifiable good of another sentient organism for no proportionate agency-protecting purpose. This route retains distinctions between human and animal capacities without treating inability to reciprocate as permission for gratuitous suffering.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the participant account's incomplete derivation of animal protection from life-relevant facts.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that moral discourse primarily coordinates and expresses deeply held attitudes, while factual reasoning informs those attitudes without creating stance-independent categorical authority.

novelty.explanation: This develops emotivism into a practical coordination account while retaining the challenge to categorical objective authority.

premises.text: Descriptions of survival, flourishing, agency, or suffering can identify consequences and instrumental relations, but no such description alone entails that every agent categorically ought to prioritize them.

novelty.explanation: This consolidates the fact-norm challenge without relying upon the weaker spatial-location formulation.

premises.text: Moral discourse characteristically expresses approval, condemnation, commitment, and demands for coordination, while remaining responsive to factual correction concerning the objects and consequences of those attitudes.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the simplistic opposition between emotion and knowledge by allowing factual reasoning to correct attitude-informed judgment.

premises.text: Persistent moral disagreement can remain after factual agreement because agents differ in ultimate attitudes, priorities, and emotional attachments, which supports an expressive account without proving every utterance purely emotive.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new argument from residual disagreement while explicitly limiting the inference to avoid overstatement.

premises.text: Rights can function as justified social conventions protecting shared interests and reducing coercive conflict even if they are not stance-independent properties that categorically bind every conceivable egoist.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the practical concern that rejecting objective morality leaves no coherent role for rights or institutional protection.

conclusion.text: Therefore, emotivism can interpret moral claims as reason-responsive expressions and coordination commitments while denying that life, flourishing, or agency supplies universally categorical moral truth conditions.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion strengthens practical coherence while limiting the denial to universally categorical, stance-independent moral authority.

newArguments.title: Reason-responsive expressivism
newArguments.text: Expressive moral discourse need not exclude reasoning. Facts can reveal that a condemned practice does not cause the believed harm, that two commitments conflict, or that a policy frustrates values its supporters already endorse. Reason then improves coherence and instrumental accuracy without discovering a categorical property of oughtness. This explains why moral argument feels substantive: participants seek factual correction, consistency, imaginative identification, and coordinated commitment, even when their ultimate motivations remain affective and no stance-independent value compels every possible agent.

novelty.explanation: This newly explains moral reasoning within expressivism and directly answers the objection that emotions cannot support knowledge or argument.

newArguments.title: Institutional rights without moral properties
newArguments.text: Rights may be defended as durable public rules that agents have powerful shared reasons to support: they reduce domination, stabilize expectations, protect planning, and permit peaceful disagreement. Their institutional justification does not require treating rights as metaphysical objects or pretending that every advantaged violator feels categorically bound. Enforcement addresses precisely those exceptional violators. This account preserves criticism, protection, and collective action while interpreting rights-language as a forceful public commitment grounded in convergent interests rather than as proof of objective moral properties.

novelty.explanation: This repairs emotivism's practical gap by explaining why rights remain defensible and enforceable without stance-independent moral properties.
